notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order grouped by theme, not a chronology; surah order is not time order. Quraysh is named in a single short passage; the draft states it and nothing more. Other passages that address the people of the Prophet's own time are not part of this inventory item.

claims.statement_en: The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh.
It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer.
It tells them to worship the Lord of this House.
It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh and of their journey of winter and summer [c1][c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh [c1]. It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer [c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House [c3]. It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear [c4].
chapters.deep_md:
- The Quran speaks of the accustoming of Quraysh (106:1) [c1].
- It speaks of their accustomed journey of winter and summer (106:2) [c2].
- It tells them to worship the Lord of this House (106:3) [c3].
- It says that He is the One who fed them against hunger and made them secure from fear (106:4) [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran reminds Quraysh of their journeys in winter and in summer [c2]. It tells them to worship the Lord of this House [c3]. He is the One who fed them and kept them safe from fear [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage ties the food and safety Quraysh enjoyed to a call to worship their Lord [c3][c4]. One reading is that the ayat ask the hearers to answer gifts with worship [c3][c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the ayat do not say where Quraysh lived, who they were or how many; the draft names no place.
- Not established: which House is meant by this House, and which journeys are meant, are not stated beyond the words of the ayat.
- Not established: how the first ayah is joined to the rest (the grammar of the opening letter) is read in more than one way; the draft states the ayat in order.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the cities, the trade routes and the House that later accounts connect with the passage; none is used here.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Quraysh and this passage. None is used in this draft.
Wording a scholar should check first: 106:1 (the accustoming, and its grammatical link to the preceding passage as some read it), 106:2 (the journey of winter and summer), 106:3 (this House).
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Makkah, the Kaaba, the routes to the south and to the north, and the tribe's history; none is used.
